english.title: Owner / person in charge of dog dangerously out of control causing injury to assistance dog

english.notes:
(i) 'Dangerously out of control' was defined in Rafiq v DPP [1997] 161 JP 412 as meaning - when there are grounds for reasonable apprehension that a dog will injure any person, whether or not it does so, if a dog causes injury without first causing anyone reasonable apprehension that it will do so, the injury itself constitutes grounds for reasonable apprehension of injury.
(ii) "Dangerously out of control" does not apply to dogs being used for lawful purposes by the police or a person in the service of the crown, therefore dogs being used lawfully by the police, prison service, military police, and customs and excise, are exempt.
(iii) In proceedings for this offence against an owner who was not in charge of the dog, it is a defence under section 3(2) to prove that the dog was, at the material time, in the charge of a person whom he reasonably believed to be fit and proper to be in charge of it.
(iv) Section 3(1B) provides a defence in 'householder cases' - i.e. the dog is in a dwelling and the person in relation to whom the dog is dangerously out of control is in, or is entering, the dwelling as a trespasser (or the defendant believed this to be the case).
(v) A court may make a destruction order and disqualify the offender from having custody of a dog ( section 4 as amended by the Dangerous Dogs (Amendment) Act 1997).
(vi) A court may make a contingent destruction order, see section 4A.
(vii) See also offence wordings H11472 (non-fatal injury to a person), H11473 (no injury) and H11474 (fatal injury to a person)

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Three years imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
